what_worked: Strong thesis about concentration; honest missingness slide with stealth-company observation was genuinely thoughtful.
fix_next: Total revenue is $15.6M not $334M—this 20x error cascades through every slide and invalidates most claims.
verdict: Compelling narrative built on a catastrophically wrong total revenue figure.
factual_error_detail: Slide 2: Total revenue stated as $334M; actual is ~$15.6M (off by ~21x). Top-10 share stated as 61%; actual is ~49.6%. Slide 3: All Pareto percentages built on the wrong $334M base; top-10 share of ~50% not 61%. Slide 5: 70% US revenue share unverifiable but plausible direction; $334M base wrong. Slide 6: E-Commerce revenue stated as $54.8M; actual is ~$1.1M. AI is actually the highest total-revenue category ($2.36M), not E-Commerce. Slide 7: Stripe revenue share stated as 96%; actual is ~86.7% ($13.5M/$15.6M). Startup share stated as 64%; actual is 63.6% (close but the revenue claim is materially wrong). Slide 8: Zero-revenue count stated as 20%; actual is 21.6% (216/1000)—close but the '10% never earned' and '$76M Stan' claims are unverifiable/likely wrong given the inflated total. Slide 9: B2B median 4x higher than B2C; actual median multiple is ~2.35x, not 4x.

evidence.insight: The power-law thesis (slides 2-3) and the missingness-as-signal idea (slide 4) show genuine analytical thinking, but insights are undermined by fabricated numbers. The AI-vs-commerce tension on slide 6 is interesting but factually inverted.
evidence.narrative: Clear arc from concentration → who wins → data gaps → takeaways. Coherent sequencing with a thesis that carries through. Slide 10 synthesizes well. Loses credit because the narrative rests on wrong numbers.
evidence.framing: Slide 1 sets context (1,000 startups, frozen date). Slide 4 addresses limitations thoughtfully. However, no mention of 274 missing category values when making category claims, and 241 missing country values when making country claims. Audience is implied but never stated.
evidence.accuracy: The foundational total revenue figure ($334M vs actual $15.6M) is wrong by a factor of ~21. This cascades: top-10 share (61% vs 49.6%), E-Commerce revenue ($54.8M vs $1.1M), Stripe revenue share (96% vs ~87%), B2B multiple (4x vs ~2.35x). Category ranking is inverted (AI is highest total, not E-Commerce). These are not rounding differences—they are order-of-magnitude errors.
evidence.visual: Gamma template with consistent dark theme. Decorative AI illustrations (cityscape, anime figure, Japanese map) add no analytical value. Charts are minimal—only two actual data visualizations (slides 3 and 6). Slide 6 chart shows only two bars (E-Commerce vs All Other) which is a poor chart choice. Donut charts on slide 7 are adequate. Heavy text density throughout.
evidence.ai_slop: Decorative AI-generated illustrations on slides 1, 2, 5 are purely aesthetic with no data connection. The anime figure on slide 2 and Japanese-themed map on slide 5 are thematically random. Consulting-style language ('uncomfortable truths,' 'cold open') is mildly inflated but not egregious.
